overview: This Senate resolution recognizes January 2026 as National Mentoring Month, aimed at raising awareness of mentoring and recruiting new mentors for young people. It describes research linking mentoring to better school attendance and grades, improved mental health, college enrollment, and lower rates of drug use and delinquency. It notes that about 40 percent of young people in the United States grow up without a mentor outside their home. The resolution thanks mentoring staff and volunteers and supports expanding quality mentoring programs and efforts to close this "mentoring gap." The Senate agreed to it on February 5, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution highlights a low-cost way to help young people succeed and encourages more adults and organizations to get involved in mentoring.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or commit any funding to mentoring programs.
